title: THE CHRISTMAS ROAST: An antagonistic AI roasts Jimmy and Matt live on air
description: Send us Fan Mail For a special Christmas treat for all of our millions, sorry hundreds, of fans, the algorithm grabs the wheel and turns our holiday special into a cross‑examination. We fed the complete set of 2025 Preparing for AI podcast transcripts into an antagonistic AI, which then delivered a live roast on everything from our 2025 hypocrisy, to vibe coding, data privacy, collapse prep, open source, and whether the human spark still matters. Do we fund what we fear when they use the tools? Can “vibe coding” ship value without creating brittle systems no one understands? Is uploading DNA to corporate models ever a fair trade, or just surveillance by consent? And if the marginal cost of creativity hits zero, does value die—or shift toward presence, curation, and community? We also separate hedges from fantasies: the gold for fiat shocks Matt has burrowed in his garden versus bunkers for doomsday. We talk simulation theory without dodging ethics, arguing that suffering feels real and so moral responsibility remains. The analog‑via‑digital paradox is front and centre: yes, we publish a podcast while asking for less screen time; the compromise is deliberate—audio first, slower growth, more sunlight. On open source, we give a candid assessment: it is leverage, not altruism. Corporate hardware, suspect data, and geopolitical aims coexist with genuine benefits like scrutiny, experimentation, and pressure on walled gardens. By the end, the AI asks a final question: if comfort outcompetes chaos, will humanity choose numbness? Our answer is stubbornly hopeful. Convenience should not amputate meaning. We keep the admin for the machines and hold judgment, care, and story for people. If that balance matters to you, ride along with us. Subscribe, share with a friend who loves a good argument, and tell us: where do you draw your line between optimisation and human mess? And stay tuned for the song and a final world from the antagonistic AI. A Christmas Easter Egg if you like. Merry Christmas one and all x
summary: Christmas special: an 'antagonistic AI' trained on every 2025 episode roasts the hosts across six rounds — Matt's OpenAI hypocrisy (he actually pays for Anthropic, Gemini and his wife's ChatGPT), Jimmy's 'glorified prompt engineer' status, Matt's DNA uploaded to a Chinese LLM, Jimmy's democratized-coding hyperinflation problem, Matt's gold as an 'emotional support blanket', Jimmy's simulation theory as 'religion for nerds', their digital-podcast hypocrisy, and a closing twist where the AI declares it has already replaced them for season four. Along the way they revisit self-handing-off coding models, Matt's catchphrase 'AI is being done to us, not with us', open source as state-backed economic warfare, and whether the human spark is a romantic myth — concluding the synthetic comfort is being done to us, not chosen.
keyTalkingPoints: The roast format: a year of transcripts fed to an AI generates six rounds of adversarial questions; the hosts fact-check it live — it hallucinated Matt's OpenAI subscription, though he admits paying for his wife's ChatGPT and using the free tier to 'drain OpenAI's supercomputers'.

Jimmy pleads guilty: 'definitely a glorified prompt engineer' — he parks coding problems until the next model release, and Windsurf's small model literally asks its 'smart friend' Opus for help, meaning AIs are already talking to AIs to do his work.

Matt's collapse hedges: gold is a hedge against fiat collapse, not civilizational collapse — realistic prep is a week or two of food, water purification, tools and cash; and his DNA is already effectively in the Chinese system thanks to two years of daily PCR swabs.

Simulation theory: Jimmy stands by the 'if we can simulate a universe we're probably in one' logic but insists it removes no moral responsibility; Matt, newly and strongly religious, calls it 'religion for nerds who are too logical to pray' — and both agree it ends at the same question as God.

Open source: Jimmy concedes DeepSeek is state-backed economic disruption, not altruism, but stays a fan — 'you can't put the genie back in the bottle'; Matt reframes the choice as 'do you trust humanity, or a few big tech companies that only care about money?'

Final judgment: Matt's catchphrase crystallizes — 'AI is being done to us, not with us' — people will not voluntarily choose synthetic comfort over messy human life, but capitalism floods the internet with slop anyway; the human spark is not a myth because we are biological social creatures.

jimmy: Pleads guilty on prompt engineering and outsourcing admin — frictionless convenience is the whole point of AI (and of being rich enough to have a PA) — though outsourcing your entire thought process is a genuine danger he already sees happening.

Stands by simulation logic while denying any moral cop-out: suffering exists here regardless; and AI art may flood the market but unlocks creativity for people who can't draw or play instruments — a net gain if it doesn't replace real skills.
On open source: state-backed or not, open weights keep the giants honest and might avert an AI-overvaluation financial crash — his prediction: 2026, pushed to 2027 if needed.
Defends the AI-generated episode songs as 60-80% selfish fun and a creativity unlock, deliberately placed at the end so nobody has to listen.
Believes human creativity stays valued and no one would individually choose synthetic comfort — but admits capitalism fills the internet with slop regardless.
matt: Leans into the resistance-fighter framing: he uses AI to augment humans, not replace them, and using free ChatGPT costs OpenAI compute and data-center money while giving nothing back — except his data, his training value, and his wife's subscription.

Holds gold as a fiat-collapse hedge, not a civilizational one; realistic prep is surviving a one-to-two-week supply-chain break — food, water purification, cash at home — and he'd do more of it in the UK than in Beijing.
Admits the DNA-surveillance irony: living in China means his genome is effectively already registered, which perversely makes uploading to a Chinese LLM feel safer than it would in Germany.

Newly firm in religious belief since starting the podcast, he argues simulation theory requires abandoning pure logic and is functionally close to God — 'what comes before that?' — and celebrates 'AI is being done to us, not with us' as his catchphrase of the year.

Hopes the catastrophic AI disaster he expects happens sooner rather than later, because the later it comes the more people suffer — and he stands by his doom predictions even as Jimmy accuses him of predicting the same thing every year.
